full_judgment:
MA Wahhab Miah J: This appeal, by leave, at the instance of the writ-respondents, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated the 30th day of June, 2002 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3609 of 2001 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The respondents herein as writ-petitioners filed the said writ petition before the High Court Division for the following relief:— 

 "(A) Issue Rule Nisi calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 shall not be directed to implement the Government decision to declare the Petitioners as Second Class gazette Government Officers as per the Gazette Notification dated 26-10-1979(Annexure-A) and/or pass such other or further order or orders as your Lordships may deem fit and proper." 

 3. The case of the writ-petitioner-respondents (hereinafter referred to as the writ-petitioners), in short, was that they were appointed in 1981 as National Savings Officers under the Ministry of Finance under the Gazette Officers (Department of National Savings, Ministry of Finance) Recruitment Rules, 1979 (hereinafter referred to as the Recruitment Rules, 1979) in the National Pay Scale of Taka 425-30-574-EB-80-735-50-1035 having fulfilled the requisite qualification of 'Bachelor's degree' preferably with economics. Since appointment, the writ-petitioners have been discharging their duties to the satisfaction of the authority. In the Recruitment Rules, 1979, the post of National Savings Officers was "termed as Gazetted Officers". The Ministry of Finance, Internal Resources Division, (the Ministry) by a Notification bearing SRO No. 514 -L/84/MFPIRD-11/NS/Admn-11/84 dated 23-8-1984 amended the Recruitment Rules, 1979, describing the 'Savings Officer' in Grade-II keeping other things intact and unchanged. In 1995, the Ministry replaced the Recruitment Rules, 1979 through a Gazette Notification under SRO No.124-Ain/95 dated 8-7-1995 wherein the Savings Officers were placed at serial No. 5 describing them as Officers (i.e. Savings Officers). 

 4. Further case of the writ-petitioners was that although they were recruited under the Recruitment Rules, 1979, they were not given the status of Second Class Gazetted Officers, which was likely to affect their future prospect and benefit. There were several correspondences by the Department with the Government and recommendations were also made for declaring the writ-petitioners as Gazetted Officers, but without any result. In the Recruitment Rules, 1979, the post of National Savings Officers was shown gazetted posts and out of the total posts, 50% were to be filled up by direct recruitment and other 50% posts were to be filled up by promotion. The Ministry informed the Accountant-General (Civil) about the up gradation of the post of officers of National Savings Department by placing them in the National Pay Scale of Taka 470-1135. The petitioners being guided by the Recruitment Rules, 1979, were entitled to be declared as Second Class Gazetted Officers. All attempt of the writ-petitioners to be treated as Second Class Gazetted Officers having failed, they through their lawyer served a notice upon the writ-respondents demanding justice by mitigating their grievance, but there was no response to the said notice; hence they filed the writ petition for the aforementioned relief and obtained the Rule. 

 5. Writ-respondent No. 4, Director-National Savings Directorate, contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that although in the Recruitment Rules, 1979, 'Saving Officers' were shown to be Gazetted Officers, they, in fact, were not Gazetted Officers since the post of Assistant Director was the immediate higher post of the Savings Officer and was a Second Class Gazetted post in the Pay Scale of Taka 625-1315 and, as such, the post of the Pay Scale of Taka 425-1035 could not be a Second Class Gazetted post. By the Notification dated June 20, 1981, the post of Savings Officers was bifurcated into Grade-I and Grade-H in the Pay Scale of Taka 470-1135 and Taka 425-1035 respectively and later on, the same was abolished and the post of Savings Officers was inserted showing the same as non-gazetted post. The writ-petitioners applied for appointment in the post of Savings Officers in the light of notification dated August 7, 1980 and as they were appointed in the non-gazetted 3rd class post, they could not claim to be 2nd Class Gazetted Officers from the date of their appointment. The proposal was made by the Ministry to the Ministry of Establishment for treating the Savings Officers as 2nd Class Gazetted Officers, but the same was turned down on May 7, 1996 observing that upgrading was not permissible and, as such, claim for declaring the writ-petitioners as 2nd Class Gazetted Officers was not entertainable in law. 

 6. A Division Bench of the High Court Division hearing the writ petition by the judgment and order dated 30-6-2002 made the Rule absolute declaring the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers since their appointment under the Recruitment Rules, 1979. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the writ-respondents filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1504 of 2002 before this Division and leave was granted on 15.05.2004 to consider the following grounds: " 

 I. Because the High Court Division failing to take into consideration the fact that the writ petitioners were appointed in the post of Savings Officers (pursuant to notification dated 7-8-1980, wherein the post had been specifically mentioned as "non-gazetted 3rd Class post" and the post of Assistant Director (which is the immediate higher post to that of the Savings Officer) was Second Class Gazetted post, erred in law in making the Rule absolute declaring the writ petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers since their appointment. 

 II. Because the Rule having been issued for direction to implement the Government decision to declare the petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers, the High Court Division erred in law in travelling beyond the terms of the Rules making the declaration that they (writ petitioners) are 2nd Class Gazetted Officers since their appointment under the Recruitment Rules, 1979. 

 III. Because the declaration in making the Rule absolute the High Court Division went beyond the scope of Article 102 of the Constitution and the High Court Division exercised its jurisdiction in making such a declaration thereby usurped the function of the executive. 

 IV. Because the Government having not taken any decision in the matter rather the proposal sent by the Ministry of Finance was turned down by the Ministry of Establishment on the ground that there is no scope to go beyond the report of the Administrative Recognition Committee, the High Court Division erred in law in ignoring the aforesaid aspect of the case thereby exceed its jurisdiction in making such declaration. 

 V. Because the writ-petitioners having been appointed as Saving Officers (in non gazetted 3rd class post) cannot claim to be 2nd Class gazetted officer and there being no decision of the Government in that regard, there cannot be any function of implementation thereof, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute." 

 8. Mr. Murad Reza, learned Additional Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the appellants, has reiterated the grounds on which leave was granted. In addition, he has further submitted that in the writ petition, the Government of Bangladesh was not made a respondent as provided in article 146 of the Constitution, the writ-petitioners were not entitled to get any relief in the writ petition and the Rule was liable to be discharged on that ground alone. He has further submitted that the writ petition was not maintainable in law as the question of gradation of the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers falls within the terms and conditions of service in the Republic and it is the Administrative Tribunal which had the exclusive jurisdiction to decide the question. He has lastly submitted that the proposals to declare the post of Savings Officers as Second Class Gazetted Officers were nothing, but inter-departmental and interministerial communications. Therefore, the writ-petitioners could not rely upon those communications for enforcement of their right of getting the status of Second Class Gazetted Officers, but the High Court Division failed to consider this legal aspect of the case and thus erred in law in making the Rule absolute declaring the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers since their appointment under the Recruitment Rules, 1979 and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside. 

 10. Let us first see the propriety of the judgment and order of the High Court Division in the light of the grounds on which leave was granted. 

 11. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division made the Rule absolute declaring the post of Savings Officers as Second Class Gazetted Officers relying upon the Recruitment Rules, 1979 on the view that as there was no 3rd Class Non-Gazetted post in the schedule to the said Rules to be filled up by the Public Service Commission and in the Rules, National Savings Officers having been shown as Second Class Gazetted, under no circumstances the post could be treated as 3rd class non-gazetted. The High Court Division further observed that the Recruitment Rules, 1979 was prepared by the President in exercise of the powers conferred on him by the proviso to articles 133 in consultation with the Public Service Commission as provided in article 140 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (the Constitution), there was no scope of deviation from the said Rules and in the Rules, the National Savings Officers, having been shown to be gazetted post, the writ-petitioners could not be treated as 3rd class non-gazetted and if that is done that will be violation of the Service Rules. The High Court Division further noticed that the Director of National Savings, writ-respondent No.4 (appellant No.4 herein) on 21-1-1985, 18-2-1985 and 22-1-1989 (annexures-'C' and 'D' series to the writ petition) recommended the case of the writ-petitioners to declare them as Second Class Gazetted Officers and also mentioned that they were drawing pay more than a Gazetted Officer and, as such, there was no involvement of additional expenditure from the Government Exchequer. The High Court Division further noticed that the Ministry of Finance also agreed to the proposal and the Ministry of Establishment on 7-3-1992 sought a formal proposal from the Ministry of Finance to formally declare 66 posts of Savings Officers to be Second Class Gazetted Officers. The High Court Division also noticed that in the similar case, the Government on 23-1-1992 declared the post of Inspectors and Superintendent of the Customs and Excise Department under the Board of Revenue as Class-I and Class-II. Thus, the writ-petitioners had been discriminated in their service in not declaring them as Gazetted Officers. The High Court Division further held that although, subsequently, the Government on 23-8-1984 by SRO No. 514-L/84/MFP/IRD-111/NS/Admn-11 /84 added new schedule to the Recruitment Rules, 1979 and the post of Savings Officers was bifurcated to Grade-I and Grade-II, but by that bifurcation, the petitioners, who were recruited under Rules, 1979, could not be affected; so also the new Rules framed in 1995 under the name and style National Savings Directorate (Officer and Employees) Recruitment Rules, 1995 (জাতীয় সঞ্চয় পরিদপ্তর কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী নিয়োগ বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৫) where the post of Savings Officers has been shown at serial No.5. 

 12. The Recruitment Rules, 1979 which was annexed to the writ petition as annexure-'A' clearly shows that in the schedule thereto there were four posts namely: (1) Chief Director, National Savings, (2) Assistant Chief Director, National Savings, (3) Assistant Director, National Savings and (4) National Savings Officers and all those four posts were Gazetted posts. In the writ petition, the petitioners specifically stated that the post of Savings Officers was 2nd Class Gazetted and this is clearly substantiated by the Recruitment Rules, 1979. It is true that in the advertisement dated 7th day of August, 1980 (annexure-'X' to the affidavit-in-opposition), pursuant to which the petitioners were appointed, the post of National Savings Officers was stated to be Non-Gazetted 3rd Class, but that was stated contrary to the said Rules. In the Recruitment Rules, 1979 under which the petitioners were appointed, there was no 3rd Class post. Therefore, there could be no reason to term the post as Non-Gazetted Third Class. And merely because in the advertisement for recruitment the post was termed as Non-Gazetted 3rd Class, it did not become so. Moreover, it is not the case of the contesting respondent that the writ-petitioners were appointed under any other Recruitment Rules or under any other administrative arrangement. 

 13. From the Recruitment Rules, 1979, it further appears that the same was made by the President in exercise of the powers conferred on him by the proviso to article 133 of the Constitution after due consultation with the Public Service Commission as mandated in article 140 thereof, so provision of the Recruitment Rules, 1979 could not be ignored. It is also necessary to state that the very title of the Recruitment Rules, 1979 is "the Gazetted Officers (Department of National Savings, Ministry of Finance) Recruitment Rules, 1979" and in the schedule thereto, the post of Savings Officers being very much there, by no logic, it can be said that the post of National Savings Officers was 3rd Class Non-Gazetted. The writ-petitioners having been appointed under the Recruitment Rules, 1979 shall definitely be guided by the said Rules. Therefore, they could not be deprived of their right to be treated as Second Class Gazetted Officers. And the respondents including the Government were under legal obligation to treat the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers. 

 14. The grounds on which leave was granted, ground Nos. I and V, are interrelated and overlapping and these two grounds relate to the point than as in the notification inviting applications for appointment to the post of Savings Officers, the post was specifically mentioned as 3rd Class Non-Gazetted and since the writ-petitioners were appointed as Non-Gazetted and the Government did not declare the said post as Second Class Gazetted, the High Court Division erred in law in giving the declaration by the impugned judgment and order, have got no merits, the reasons already assigned hereinbefore. 

 15. Another corollary point to the above grounds of the appellants that the post of Assistant Director (which was the immediate higher post to that of the Savings Officers) being Second Class, the post of Savings Officers, could not be Second Class Gazetted, is absolutely fallacious because there cannot be any bar in having two posts in the same class having two different ranks. For example, the Assistant Secretary and the Secretary of a Ministry both are class one officers but they hold two different ranks; further when the Recruitment Rules, 1979 clearly made the post of Savings Officers as Second Class Gazetted by no argument or logic the same could be treated otherwise, that is, 3rd class. The Recruitment Rules, 1979 under which the writ-petitioners were appointed gave them the right to be treated as Second Class Gazetted Officers; the Government could not deny their said right so the failure of the Government to take decision in the matter in favour of the writ-petitioners, cannot create any bar in deciding the merit of the claim of the petitioners. 

 16. In so far as ground Nos. II, III and IV are concerned, it appears that Rule was issued as per term of the prayer made in the writ petition calling upon the writ-respondents to show cause as to why respondent Nos. 1 and 2 shall not be directed to implement the Government decision to declare the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers as per the Gazette Notification for the ends of justice. But the High Court Division itself declared the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers. It is a fact that although there were internal correspondences amongst the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Establishment and the Director, National Savings Directorate to give the writ-petitioners the status of Second Class Gazetted Officers, but no final decision was taken by the Government in that respect. Rather respondent No. 4 in his affidavit-in-opposition has categorically stated that the Ministry of Establishment by its Memo dated 7-5-1996 turned down the proposal holding that "It is not possible to upgrade the post beyond the report of the Administrative structure" and has annexed the said Memo as annexure-'X(3)'. 

 17. Now, the question is whether the High Court Division was justified in giving the declaration beyond the Rule issuing order. The prayer of the writ-petition has been quoted hereinbefore which prima facie shows that the writ-petitioners made the prayer to direct respondent Nos. 1 and 2 to implement the Government decision to declare them as Second Class Gazetted Officers as per the Gazette Notification dated 26-10-1979. Therefore, there was no scope of giving the relief by way of declaration as has been given by the High Court Division. In this regard, we like to observe that the prayer to the effect "and/or such other of further order or orders as your Lordships may deem fit and proper" do not authorize a writ Court to give relief beyond the Rule issuing order, such prayer authorizes the writ Court to give any incidental relief or reliefs which may follow from the main relief according the Rule issuing order. But in the instant case when the main prayer was made as to why respondent Nos. 1 and 2 shall not be directed to implement the Government decision to declare the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers and, in fact, there was no Government decision in that respect, rather respondent No. 4 claimed that the Government through the Ministry of Establishment vide annexure-'X3' refused to upgrade the post, the question of implementing the Government decision declaring the writ-petitioners as Second Class Gazetted Officers does not arise at all. So, we find merits in ground Nos. II, III and IV. 

 18. Now, the additional points urged by the learned Additional Attorney-General. It is also a fact that the writ-petitioners did not make the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the concerned Ministry, a party in the writ petition as provided in article 146 of the Constitution, instead they made the respective secretaries of the Ministry of Establishment, the Ministry of Finance (Finance Division) and the Secretary Ministry of Internal Resources Division as respondents. From the impugned judgment and order as well as the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the contesting respondent No.4, it does not appear that any objection as to the non-impleading of the Government of Bangladesh in proper form as respondent in the writ petition, was taken. Had such objection been taken before the High Court Division, the writ-petitioners could have taken step to cure the defect by making necessary amendment in the cause title of the petition. In the leave petition as well as in the concise statement filed by the appellant, no such point has also been taken. 

 19. In similar way, the maintainability of the writ petition on the ground of availability of the alternative efficacious remedy before the Administrative Tribunal was also neither taken in the affidavit-in-opposition nor at the time of hearing of the Rule and also in the leave petition and the concise statement. According to the provisions of Order XX, rule 5 of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (Appellate Division) Rules, 1988 the appellants were not legally entitled to argue the above points. But the learned Additional Attorney-General argued those points with our leave. 

 20. Be that as it may, let us see the soundness of the additional points urged by the learned Additional Attorney-General. So far as the submission as to the non-impleading of the Government of Bangladesh in the writ petition is concerned, it is a fact that the Government of Bangladesh was not made a party within the meaning of article 146 of the Constitution. And we state the position of law that the respective secretaries of the respective ministries as impleaded in the writ petition could not represent the Government of Bangladesh unless it was made party as provided in article 146 of the Constitution. At the same time, the responsibility of a contesting party to raise the point in the affidavit-in-opposition or at the time of hearing of the Rule before the High Court Division and even before this Division when the leave petition was heard and in the concise statement as well could not altogether be condoned. The contesting party also owed a duty to the Court to raise such point so that the Court could answer the same. So far as the other point, namely, the internal correspondences amongst the Ministries and the parent department, is concerned, it appears that the High Court Division in making the Rule absolute also relied upon those correspondences, though those were not at all necessary. In this regard, we also state the position of law that the internal correspondences amongst the Ministries and the parent department cannot be the sole basis to give rise to a cause of action to ventilate the grievance of a party. As the point of maintainability of the writ petition on the ground of availability of the efficacious remedy before the Administrative Tribunal was not taken before the High Court Division, it had no chance to dwell upon the same. However, in the facts and circumstances of the instant case and the merits of the claim of the writ-petitioners as discussed above, we do not consider it necessary to dwell on the point of maintainability. And since we have found that the writ-petitioner-respondents acquired the right to be treated as Second Class Gazetted Officers as per provision of the Recruitment Rules, 1979 under which they were appointed; we are not inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment and order in order to do complete justice to the writ-petitioners invoking our power under article 104 of the Constitution. We further direct the Government of Bangladesh through the writ-respondent-appellants to give the writ-petitioner-respondents the status of Second Class Gazetted Officers immediately from the date of their appointment as Savings Officers.
